subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep `bootstrap-extra-files` limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: This changes deterministic system-prompt context and the file-loading trust boundary, so maintainer product intent is required before the implementation lands.

options.title: Approve bounded hook contract
options.body: Allow in-workspace custom-basename files through the existing hook path after a linked PR or replacement preserves guards, budgets, filtering, and docs.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and document the supported workaround using existing recognized bootstrap files.

options.title: Defer to broader context API
options.body: Keep the current restriction until a broader context-loading API defines discovery, trust, and session scoping.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded hook contract
recommendation.body: Allow in-workspace custom-basename files through the existing hook path after a linked PR or replacement preserves guards, budgets, filtering, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent boundary-safe bootstrap read history in the affected loader surface.
